title: Air India to Move New York JFK Operations to New Terminal 6 in 2028
excerpt: The airline will become the 16th international carrier at the $4.2 billion terminal, where it plans to open its first flagship Maharaja Lounge in North America's busiest Indian aviation corridor.
body:
• Air India will relocate from JFK Terminal 4 to the new Terminal 6 in 2028, joining 15 other international carriers at the $4.2 billion facility.
  • The airline will open its first flagship Maharaja Lounge at JFK, spanning 9,100 square feet with views of the terminal's commercial concourse.
  • Terminal 6 houses multiple Star Alliance partners, enabling same-terminal connections to destinations across the Americas for Air India passengers.
  • The move is part of JFK's $19 billion airport-wide redevelopment and Air India's own transformation following its 2022 privatisation.

Air India has announced it will move its New York operations from John F. Kennedy International Airport's Terminal 4 to the new Terminal 6 starting in 2028, marking one of the most significant upgrades to the airline's presence in its busiest North American market.

The carrier will become the 16th international airline to commit to Terminal 6, joining fellow Star Alliance members including Lufthansa, Air Canada, All Nippon Airways, Austrian Airlines, SWISS and TAP Air Portugal, as well as JetBlue, Cathay Pacific, Aer Lingus, Icelandair and others.

Maharaja Lounge Comes to New York

As part of the transition, Air India will open its first flagship Maharaja Lounge at JFK Terminal 6. The 9,100-square-foot lounge will be located in a post-security area overlooking the terminal's commercial concourse and will showcase the airline's signature Indian hospitality. The announcement follows the recent opening of a Maharaja Lounge at San Francisco International Airport.

"New York has long been one of India's most important global gateways; it's a relationship that spans more than six decades. Our move to Terminal 6 will complement the deployment of our flagship aircraft offering the 'new Air India experience' to our customers."

— Campbell Wilson, CEO and Managing Director, Air India

Wilson added that Terminal 6's design, operational efficiency and proximity to other Star Alliance carriers would enable "smoother, seamlessly connected journeys through JFK starting in 2028."

Star Alliance Under One Roof

The co-location with Star Alliance partners is a key strategic advantage. Passengers connecting between Air India and airlines such as Lufthansa, Air Canada or ANA will be able to make transfers within the same terminal, eliminating the need to navigate JFK's notoriously complex inter-terminal system.

Air India currently operates daily nonstop flights from JFK Terminal 4 to Delhi and Mumbai, deploying its Airbus A350 and Boeing 777 aircraft on the routes. Operations at Terminal 4 will continue until the transition is complete.

A New Terminal for a New JFK

Terminal 6 is being developed by JFK Millennium Partners — a consortium led by Vantage Group alongside RXR and JetBlue — as part of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey's $19 billion redevelopment of JFK Airport. The project is opening in phases, with the first gates becoming operational in 2026 and the full ten-gate terminal expected by 2028. Nine of the ten gates will accommodate widebody aircraft.

The terminal has been designed around what its developers call a "boutique-style" passenger experience, featuring shorter walking distances from TSA screening to gates, intuitive wayfinding, modern amenities and a curated retail and dining programme reflecting New York's character.

"Air India's decision to join Terminal 6 validates the innovative approach we have taken to create and manage a new world-class international terminal at JFK."

— George Casey, Chair, JFK Millennium Partners and CEO, Vantage Group

Part of Air India's Broader Transformation

The Terminal 6 commitment reflects Air India's wider overhaul since its privatisation and acquisition by Tata Group in 2022. The airline has embarked on a comprehensive transformation programme that includes fleet renewal backed by record orders for 600 aircraft, new cabin products across all classes, digital enhancements and a rapidly expanding international network.

The JFK lounge and terminal upgrade signal that the airline is investing not just in its fleet but in the ground experience — an area where Air India had historically lagged behind competitors on premium routes.

For the estimated 350,000 passengers who fly between New York and India annually, the move promises a measurably improved journey through one of the world's busiest airports.
nri_angle: The Terminal 6 move directly benefits the hundreds of thousands of Indian Americans who fly the New York–Delhi and New York–Mumbai routes annually. A dedicated 9,100-square-foot Maharaja Lounge and same-terminal Star Alliance connections will materially improve the travel experience on one of the diaspora's most-flown corridors.
